title: Injective-resolution representative of the derived etale/pro-etale comparison unit
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ for the abelian categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and let $
u_T^*\dashv
u_{T,*}$ be the module adjunction of the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with $
u_T^*$ exact [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. For a cochain complex $M$ of $\mathcal A$ let $\eta^0_M:M	o
u_{T,*}
u_T^*M$ be the termwise unit of this adjunction, a morphism of complexes. Let $Q$ denote localization at the quasi-isomorphisms, let $R
u_{T,*}:D^+(\mathcal B)	o D^+(\mathcal A)$ be the bounded-below right derived functor of $
u_{T,*}$ with its comparison $\alpha_N:Q(
u_{T,*}N)	o R
u_{T,*}(QN)$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], and let $\eta^D:\mathrm{id}	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*$ be the unit of the derived adjunction $
u_T^*\dashv R
u_{T,*}$ on $D^+$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], where $
u_T^*$ acts termwise.

Let $M$ be a bounded-below complex of $\mathcal A$ and let $j:
u_T^*M	o J$ be a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded-below complex $J$ of injective objects of $\mathcal B$. Then
$$
R
u_{T,*}(Qj)\circ\eta^D_{QM}=\alpha_J\circ Q igl(
u_{T,*}(j)\circ\eta^0_M igr):QM\longrightarrow R
u_{T,*}(QJ).
$$
Since $R
u_{T,*}(Qj)$ and $\alpha_J$ are isomorphisms, the morphism of complexes $
u_{T,*}(j)\circ\eta^0_M:M	o
u_{T,*}J$ represents the derived unit $\eta^D_{QM}$ under the identification $R
u_{T,*}(Qj)^{-1}\circ\alpha_J:Q(
u_{T,*}J)\xrightarrow{\sim}R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*(QM)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0DVC (label lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and Lemma Tag 09T5 (label lemma-derived-adjoint-functors): the derived adjunction bijection, whose unit at M is the transpose of the identity of the resolved inverse image; this representative is written out in the agent proof of thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison (its third step), which is not part of that node's statement.

proof.text:
Put $L=
u_T^*$, $R=
u_{T,*}$ and $\mathbf R R=R
u_{T,*}$. These act on the two abelian module categories in the statement, with their specified constant coefficients. The site adjunction is additive, and $L$ is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Thus $L$ acts termwise on $D^+$, preserving quasi-isomorphisms and lower bounds. For any bounded-below injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal B$, [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] makes $I$ K-injective, and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $RI$ K-injective. Both remain bounded below. The pro-etale coefficient ring sheaf is a sheaf of commutative rings on a small site, so $\mathcal B$ is a Grothendieck abelian category by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]; this is the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] for $v=R$. The natural comparison $\alpha_I:Q(RI)	o\mathbf R R(QI)$ is therefore defined and invertible by clause (2) of that lemma.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); explicit bounded-below Hom calculation

proof.text:
For a bounded-below complex $P$ in $\mathcal A$ and an $I$ as in step 1, use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] at $I$ and $RI$, and the explicit Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Their composite is
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\mathcal B)}(QLP,QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K^+(\mathcal B)}(LP,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K^+(\mathcal A)}(P,RI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\mathcal A)}(QP,QRI).$$
Explicitly, the unique homotopy class $[f]$ with $Q[f]=h$ is sent to $Q[Rf\circ\eta^0_P]$. Each factor is bijective. Naturality in a chain map $a:P'\to P$ follows from $RL(a)\eta^0_{P'}=\eta^0_Pa$; naturality in a map $k:I\to I'$ follows from $R(kf)=Rk\,Rf$. The termwise adjunction lemma guarantees that these expressions depend only on homotopy classes.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); explicit bounded-below Hom calculation

proof.text:
For any bounded-below $N$ in $\mathcal B$, take a bounded-below injective resolution $r:N\to I$ using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], on the small ringed pro-etale site. Put $e_r=\mathbf R R(Qr)^{-1}\alpha_I$. Postcomposition by $Qr$, the bijection in step 2, and postcomposition by $e_r$ give the derived transpose to $\mathbf R R(QN)$. Check its normalization and independence explicitly. For another resolution $r':N'\to I'$ and $b:QN\to QN'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $k:I\to I'$ with $Qk=Qr'\,b\,(Qr)^{-1}$. Naturality of the comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] says
$$\alpha_{I'}Q(Rk)=\mathbf R R(Qk)\alpha_I,$$
so $e_{r'}Q(Rk)=\mathbf R R(b)e_r$. Together with step 2 this proves target naturality; setting $b=1$ proves independence of resolution. Source naturality holds first on homotopy morphisms by step 2 and then on their inverses at quasi-isomorphisms, since $L$ preserves those; these generate the localized morphisms. Thus these are the natural Hom bijections obtained by deriving the given termwise adjunction with the specified comparison $\alpha$, namely the canonical derived adjunction in the statement. This calculates its Hom bijection, rather than deducing a normalization from full faithfulness alone.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); explicit bounded-below Hom calculation

proof.text:
The unit of an adjunction is the transpose of the identity of its left-adjoint image. Apply the explicit derived transpose from steps 2–3 at $P=M$, $N=LM$, with the given resolution $r=j$. The identity of $QLM$ is first sent to $Qj$, whose unique homotopy lift is $[j]$. Its termwise transpose is $[Rj\circ\eta^0_M]$, by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Hence the unit $\eta^D$ of the canonical derived adjunction named in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] satisfies
$$\eta^D_{QM}=\mathbf R R(Qj)^{-1}\alpha_J\,Q(Rj\circ\eta^0_M).$$
Multiplying on the left by $\mathbf R R(Qj)$ gives precisely
$$\mathbf R R(Qj)\circ\eta^D_{QM}=\alpha_J\circ Q\bigl(R(j)\circ\eta^0_M\bigr).$$
Here $L(QM)=Q(LM)$ is the termwise exact-functor identification fixed in the statement; no extra comparison is silently inserted.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives); explicit bounded-below Hom calculation

proof.text: Because $j$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $Qj$ is invertible by the definition of localization, and a functor sends an inverse to an inverse. Thus $\mathbf R R(Qj)$ is invertible. Since $J$ is bounded below with injective terms, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] makes $\alpha_J$ invertible. Therefore $e_j=\mathbf R R(Qj)^{-1}\alpha_J$ is the displayed isomorphism in the statement, and the equality in step 4 says exactly that the complex map $Rj\circ\eta^0_M$ represents the derived unit under $e_j$.
